pr_title: Fix a couple of JsonConstructor bugs & clean up JsonParameterInfo implementation.
pr_body:
Fix #60082. Fix #68647.

Simplifies the `JsonParameterInfo` implementation using conventions already used in `JsonTypeInfo` and `JsonPropertyInfo`.

issue_context.title: Default value for optional ctor params should be used when matching prop is ignored
comments: should we consider this for 6.0? it might lead to data loss

> should we consider this for 6.0? it might lead to data loss

Is this a regression from 5.0 behavior?

> Is this a regression from 5.0 behavior?

No this behavior shipped in 5.0. A fix for this can be considered a breaking change. I recommend addressing early in 7.0 as a bug fix so we have time to react to any feedback.

review_comments: Replaces `Initialize` methods with constructors -- makes it easier to guarantee non-nullability of properties.
make sure we have a test with null and IgnoreNullTokensOnRead making sure we use default value for that case (assuming that's even possible)
Seems that we don't test for that. I've added a test even though it's not in scope for this change.
My thoughts exactly :-)
this is ugly 😄 is there an issue against Type.DefaultValue about it? Why is that necessary?

Yep. It's unfortunate but necessary because the method is being used against the source generator's System.Reflection wrappers around Roslyn symbols. These checks are simply not applicable in that world.
is ShouldDeserialize still used?
It is, the converters are consulting it when deserializing constructor parameters.
